titles: Design of KENIA's Innovation Fellowship Project
descriptions:
This project seeks to provide talented young graduates in Kenya with the opportunities to practically apply their skills to real-world problems in a way that is innovative, sustainable and low-cost and will help to address societal challenges. This will be through exposure to domain experts and mentorship and through engagement with public and private sector as well as civil society. In the first-year challenges will be picked from the public sector to standardize the processes and manage the scope, with a focus on digital transformation challenges.
The specific objectives of the project include:
Key Area 1: Co-creation and design of the Innovation Fellowship Scheme
Key Area 2: Production of an Innovation Fellowship Manual, which includes Curriculum Development, Training Modules, Mentorship guide and MEL framework

titles: Corporate Startup Linkage Project (Qhala)
descriptions: Qhala, in partnership with the UK Tech Hub, successfully completed the pilot for the Corporate-Startup linkages programme dubbed iHelix, which was launched in December 2021 and ended in May 2022.  iHelix denotes the exchange of DNA between startups and corporates. This programme was aimed at bolstering partnerships and linkages by leveraging on the agility of startups in Kenya and the robust ecosystems that exist around corporates. This project was initiated following a round-table discussion that brought together 5 of the leading corporates in Kenya, who identified a few pain points in their businesses. A major issue that came out was the differences in culture, expectations and lack of trust between corporates and startups. Corporates felt that startups expectations did not match with reality and would threaten to sue over “ideas” and startups felt that corporates were stealing their ideas without compensation. This resulted in a successful pilot of this project and the current phase of the project is informed by key learnings of the pilot, with expansion to Rwanda.

titles: Institutional Commercialization Support Phase 2 (ACTS)
descriptions: The goal of phase II of this project is to strengthen and streamline the systems and processes within the selected institutions (from phase 1) towards successful commercialisation of their research outputs with a desired outcome of promoting innovation to drive job creation, increase employability, and social-economic growth. The specific objectives of this project are: a. Development and identification of relevant criteria to select first four (4) institutions to operationalize the interventions from Phase I and those proposed in phase II. b. Co-development of a practical implementation plan for each of the institutions to guide recommended interventions c. Support the institutions to implement interventions for commercialization systems in a pragmatic, sustainable and inclusive way d. Co-organize stakeholder consultations for networking, learning to draw out key lessons for wider dissemination across institutions e. Support the development of an M&E framework to be used by KeNIA and the respective institutions to keep the TTOs well supervised and accountable.

descriptions:
Phase-III of the UNJPSP, guided by the Revised National Social Protection Policy (2025) 
UNICEF, FAO and WFP will provide technical assistance to GRZ for a period of three years. 
Spanning across three pillars, this assistance has been designed to improve both the

descriptions: To provide better measures of poverty for monitoring progress towards the UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), and so give policy-makers better guidance on where and how to address extreme poverty.   The Oxford Policy and Human Development Initiative (OPHI) has collated data from hundreds of national surveys.  With DFID funding, OPHI will process this data to produce global, national and sub-national analysis of trends and patterns in multi-dimensional poverty in over 100 countries.  This will be published by the UN and provide donors, governments and NGOs with information they need to design and target policies for reducing extreme poverty.

titles: Iraq: Reform, Reconstruction and Recovery World Bank multi donor trust fund
descriptions: This project has two prinicple aims:  1. To deliver effective reconstruction and recovery spending by the World Bank and Government of Iraq; this follows the territorial defeat of Daesh, which has left Iraq with a $88 billion reconstruction bill.   2. To improve Government of Iraq efforts to achieve long-term economic and governance reform, addressing the underlying drivers which led to the emergence of Daesh.  As a result of this project, reconstruction and recovery spending by the World Bank and the Government of Iraq will be spent well, improving the lives of citizens across Iraq, in particular women and girls, and addressing the underlying drivers of instability, violent extremism and conflict.

titles: Kelp Aquaculture Development Phase 2: Enabling the commercial cultivation of African Kelp in Southern Africa West Coast region
descriptions:
Kelp Aquaculture Development Phase 2: Understanding and testing the requirements for enabling the commercial cultivation of African Kelp along Southern Africa’s West Coast region

Phase 1 of the project, (completed between January and March 2022), served as the pre-feasibility and demonstrated important results in a short time frame by identifying positive potential for kelp farming in South Africa to be further explored and confirmed in Phase 2. Phase 1 of the study identified suitable areas where Kelp could be farmed around South Africa, produced an extensive report on the biological and economic feasibility of kelp farming, tested the nutritional value of kelp and built local hatchery capacity to produce the microscopic stages of kelps for further grow-out. titles: Generate research to map and better understand conflict and atrocity prevention
descriptions: The have been several recent efforts to map and synthesise the literature assessing the effectiveness of conflict and atrocity prevention interventions. The Conflict, Stability and Security Fund recently produced an evidence review looking at what works to address conflict and instability, covering areas such as conflict resolution, governance and information campaigns. descriptions: Study investigating the community-diffusion element of the Toose Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention model delivered by FCDO Zimbabwe’s Stopping Abuse and Female Exploitation (SAFE) programme in Harare.The SAFE programme is focussed on prevention and response to violence against women, in line with the UK’s International Development Strategy, Africa Strategy and recently launched International Women and Girls Strategy. titles: Acute Humanitarian Need
descriptions: In 2014, Daesh’s expansion across Iraq set ablaze a major humanitarian crisis, compelling the UK to respond to acute needs, and also to join the counter-Daesh global coalition.  Daesh has now been defeated as a territory-holding force, and increasing numbers of people have returned home.  However, the situation is precarious, and complex humanitarian needs remain for many.    From 2019-2022, DFID Iraq will respond to the acute needs of the most vulnerable, address the complex needs of high-risk protracted caseloads, promote responsible transition to national-led efforts, and fund enabling activities crucial to achieving this.   The funding envelope for this programme reflects that DFID Iraq is planning for the best, but preparing for the worst – a seemingly optimistic trajectory one month may belie a precarious situation the next.  DFID Iraq will monitor any deterioration, setting trigger points to indicate if or when we will approach ministers for any critical change in approach.

titles: Funding for the AT Scale Partnership
descriptions: ATscale, the Global Partnership for Assistive Technology, was launched at the July 2018 Global Disability Summit and aims to catalyse access to assistive technology for 500 million more people by 2030. Assistive technology (AT) is an umbrella term covering the products, systems, and services related to the delivery of assistive products. The five priority products for ATscale are wheelchairs, eyeglasses, hearing aids, prosthetics, and personal digital assistants. The partnership’s aims are to bring market shaping approaches that have been successfully used over the last decade to cut prices and increase access to life-saving health commodities such as medicines, vaccines and contraceptives. ATscale has a twin-track approach: i) to develop an enabling environment for increased access to high-quality, affordable AT by growing political will, advocating for, and informing policy reform, mobilising investment, and strengthening systems and service delivery at global, regional, and country levels, and ii) uses market shaping interventions to make AT product markets more effective. Interventions in the market for each of the priority products will be guided by product narratives that identify the market barriers and opportunities for intervention.

Identify interventions required to Shape Markets and overcome supply and demand-side barriers for priority AT. ATscale already works at global level and is choosing countries for in-depth support. The priority products for ATscale are wheelchairs, glasses, hearing aids, prosthetics and orthotics, and digital devices. This delivers on a commitment at the Global Disability Summit in July 2018.

ICF - Veterinary Vaccine Manufacturing and Innovation centre (Vet-VMIC),
descriptions:
The Centre for Veterinary Vaccine Innovation & Manufacturing (CVIM) has been set up to bridge a gap between basic research and late-stage product development of vaccines. New technology (for example RNA vaccines) has the potential to transform vaccine development, but currently low-cost livestock vaccines utilising emerging technology are not being developed for deployment in developing countries. The overall objective of the centre is to accelerate the development and production of vaccines for the most challenging, and urgent livestock diseases, including those that can spread to humans (zoonotic diseases) and cause significant productivity loss in Low- and Middle-income Countries (LMICs).
By accelerating the development of novel vaccines for high consequence livestock diseases with commercial partners in both developed and developing countries, the programme will improve vaccine access and use and consequently improve the livelihoods of livestock farmers and economic wellbeing and food security in LIDCs. It will enable international trade and protect human health.

titles: Project Soteria: stopping perpetrators of sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment from working in the aid sector.
descriptions:
Programme aims: to support organisations in the aid sector to stop perpetrators of sexual exploitation and abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH) from working in the aid sector via more and better criminal records checks on staff and by strengthening cooperation between Law Enforcement Agencies (LEAs) and aid organisations. Strong vetting of highly mobile aid organisation’s staff is required to safeguard beneficiaries and staff against SEAH. 
Phase 1 (2019-2021) built key stakeholder relationships and designed the scope of the current implementation phase (2021-2026) which focuses on the following activities: 1. Capacity building for Law Enforcement to use INTERPOL capabilities more effectively, as well as actions such as criminal record keeping and monitoring, particularly of sexual offenders, and building understanding of SEAH in aid work; 2. Promoting information sharing, e.g. using INTERPOL Notices, to gather and disseminate intelligence internationally and reinforce border management capacity to assess and use information; 3. Criminal Analysis and Investigative Support including using a Criminal Analysis File (CAF) to develop a wider understanding of the nature, location and patterns of SEAH by aid sector staff to help inform prevention and response measures; 4. Assistance to the aid sector to help them collaborate more closely with law enforcement communities to jointly tackle SEAH; 5. Threat Identification Scheme (TIS) pilot to allow aid sector organisations to send INTERPOL information on newly hired candidates to identify individuals that could pose a risk to vulnerable adults and children; 6. Digital solutions via the Vulnerable Communities Secure Collaborative Platform to i) ingest misconduct data, ii) ingest CVs and other searchable data to check candidates and iii) share non-operational data; and 7. An Incident Response Team (IRT) to support Law Enforcement Agencies in humanitarian emergencies if requested and/or consented by a Member Country.
